memory_candidates.content: In this repo's literature extension, literature-ingest-online.sh's create-item path passes TITLE/AUTHORS_JSON/YEAR_JSON from the discovery record to check_duplicate_title() and patch_global_index() only -- never to Zotero item creation itself. zotero-write.sh item-add only accepts --pdf/--doi (wrapping `zot add`), so an arXiv-only record (no DOI) creates a metadata-less Zotero item even though richer metadata is already in hand from Semantic Scholar. Any metadata-resolution upgrade (e.g. translation-server) needs a NEW zotero-write.sh operation that posts a full JSON item body directly, since the existing item-add cannot carry one.

Zotero's Web API attach flow creates the child attachment metadata record in one call, then uploads bytes in a second call; when the account is over its storage quota, the upload is rejected with a 413 but the metadata-record call is never rolled back, leaving an orphaned, file-less attachment child item behind. Since there is no Web API endpoint for querying quota state (only the human-only account page, or a 413's error message), the only viable gate is reactive: parse used/limit MB out of a 413's error message, cache it, and skip future attach attempts pre-emptively while the cache says over-quota -- this is what actually prevents the orphan-creation side effect, since a skipped attempt never reaches the two-step create-then-upload sequence.

The zotero-cli-cc `zot` CLI (>=0.10.0) ships `zot delete KEY` (move to trash), `zot orphans clean` ("Delete orphaned attachment records via the Web API" -- purpose-built for cleaning up file-less attachment records left by a rejected upload), `zot trash list/restore`, and `zot duplicates --by doi|title|both` (working, library-wide dedup finder). All of these are local-SQLite reads/writes exactly like zot's other read commands (search/read/stats), so they are subject to the same sync-lag limitation: an item or attachment created via the Web API is invisible to them until a Zotero desktop client syncs it down. Verified live: `zot orphans list` returned zero orphans hours after two real orphaned attachment records were created via the Web API in a same-day prior task, because the local DB (`zot stats` still reporting the pre-creation item count) had not yet synced.
